strategies.name: support_to_resistance_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: After letting the first 5 to 15 minutes pass on the 5-minute chart to identify support, enter a scalp when price comes down into a support area and bounces. The examples use moving-average support such as the 13 EMA or 200 EMA, with the general rule to buy at support/demand.
strategies.exit_summary: Take profit quickly into the next resistance or after the immediate bounce; the speaker repeatedly emphasizes getting in and out fast, taking profit without overstaying. Risk/management is framed as small quick moves rather than holding for extended runs.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: enter when price comes down to the 13 EMA acting as support and bounces
variants.target_note: exit on the quick push up into nearby resistance / after several green candles
variants.transcript_quote: this 13 EMA operated as a initial support

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: enter when the 13 EMA loses support status and price bounces from the deeper 200 EMA support
variants.target_note: ride it to resistance and exit
variants.transcript_quote: another quick Scout this one off a deeper support sitting at the 200 EMA once the 13 EMA gave up its support status

strategies.name: support_breakdown_short_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: Once a key support level is lost, enter in the direction of the breakdown to catch the bigger move lower. The example specifically shows entering after price loses the 200 EMA support.
strategies.exit_summary: Cover quickly after the sharp downside extension rather than holding indefinitely; the speaker marks the end of the fast drop as the exit for the 'big scalp.'

enumeration_note: The video teaches two distinct, opposing executable scalps: buy support bounces into resistance, and short after support breaks; different EMA levels are variants of the support-bounce skeleton, not separate strategies.
